questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Distance, academic opportunities and an interesting city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was good since Freie Universitet was very easy to get in touch with.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had orientation days for all erasmus-students and at the Political Science institute.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The course system was hard to understand even after orientation since exchange students do not follow the same structure at the home students.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was alright. Use FaceBook groups ("Dansker i Berlin") to find apartments.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The travel time to the University can be long (aprox 1 hour). It can make sense to have fewer days on campus but with more lectures.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration was a bit tricky since the University works with another structure. Furthermore, online you could only register for courses within your institut. If you wanted to do courses on other institutes, you had to show up for a class and hope to get a spot in the class. Finally, it can be hard to find the information needed to do pre-approval etc. in the course catalogue. Many courses does not have a lecture plan or syllabus.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were in touch with the erasmus-arrival team and our institute.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of classes that i had found interesting but did not attend since I could not just register online. However, I got a spot in all of the courses i had registered me in that i really wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Talk to other exchange students about the registration. 
Don't get confused when the home students does not follow the same ECTS-structure. 
Show up to as many courses as you like before the registration ends so you can get to know which courses you are really interested in.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level varied between courses. Some courses really depended on BA-knowledge where others where introductions to specific fields of academic thus more independent from general BA in political science.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different from the style of teaching at UCPH. The teaching on Freie Universitet revolves around active student participation. The students at Freie participate actively in all classes and the Professors expect that a discussion is started. I liked to try this style of teaching as it forces the student to really think about the syllabus and form an opinion on the texts and topics. However, some time are "wasted" on non-academic student discussions if the Professor does not moderate the debate. Sometimes we really did not get to discuss the syllabus in depth as discussions on only one text got too long.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Passionate politics. The far right in Europe and beyond (30216a) - Sociology 
Introduction to social and religious movements (30233a) - Sociology
International Cooperation in Historical Perspective (15494) - John F. Kennedy Institute for North American Studies
Redistribution and Inequality: The United States in Comparative Perspective (32510a) - John F. Kennedy Institute for North American Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all the courses I attended as i really learned something while the courses all drew on knowledge and syllabus from the BA-level. It was fun to use theories that I were already familiar with on knew perspectives and expand the theories.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There was no unexpected costs. However, I used more money on traveling with my new friends than i have expected. Furthermore, I had some problems with my recommendation so I had to spend some money on that to.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Public transport was less expensive. 
Museums and other sightseeing was more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many atchletic acitivies, and many cultural activities especially in the introduction days. However, I did not attend.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Going on one of the trips for the erasmus-students in the first days to meet new people. 
Attend the athletic activities and the german class.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Visit the different districts in the city.
Visit Grunewald and the many lakes.
Use the Semesterticket to travel around Germany: Dresden, Munich, Leipzig etc.
Visit museums with student-discount.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was very easy. The only thing was figuring out how to address the teachers at the beginning.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
The local students were very nice and open. Maybe ask some practical questions and hope the conversations evolves. 
Alternatively, learn som German and get a local tandem-partner.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That the teachers expected us to actively participate and speak in class.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People at the university are very open and respective of each other. In general, the Germans are sweet and more talkative.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The administrative burden of an exchange is big so it's very nice to have someone to consult with and have patience. It will be worth the trouble.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You should talk to your professors about the requirements for your exams and how many ECTS-credits you can get as you do not follow the same structure as the local students. In general, the teachers and the administration are helpful but the system can be confusing and the rules vary from institute to institute.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met some really nice people and enjoyed living in Berlin. It's a wonderful city to live in and so easy to get around. I also found the teaching style interesting and really learned something and met some dedicated students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The administration and managing school, homework, work, and socialising with new people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
